elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a meta-analysis (systematic review) of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.

elements.quote: However, the trend of reinfection rate over time is not clear. ... to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract states the review objective: to estimate the global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate and its trend over time.

elements.quote: We searched ... for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract mentions eligible study designs but does not state other key inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., reinfection definition, minimum sample size, exclusions).

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang ... up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources (seven databases) and the search end date (March 16, 2023).

elements.quote: The risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk-of-bias assessment methods used.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, country, study type, and study population, and time-varying reinfection rates of SARS-CoV-2 were estimated using meta-regression.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the synthesis methods: meta-analysis, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression.

elements.quote: A total of 55 studies involving 111,846 cases of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of studies (55) and reinfection cases (111,846), but not the total participants (14,681,235, reported only in the main text) and gives limited study characteristics.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%). In the subgroup analyses, there were statistically significant differences in the pooled reinfection rates by reinfection variant, and study type ( P < 0.05).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (pooled reinfection rate) and subgroup findings.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: In the subgroup analyses, there were statistically significant differences in the pooled reinfection rates by reinfection variant, and study type ( P < 0.05).
elements.reason: The abstract notes significant subgroup differences but does not report the direction of effect or which groups had higher/lower rates (e.g., Omicron higher than other variants is only stated qualitatively in the Conclusion).
The abstract does not mention any limitations of the included evidence; limitations appear only in the Discussion/Funding sections of the main text.

elements.quote: SARS-CoV-2 is at risk of reinfection and the Omicron variant has a higher reinfection rate than other currently known variants. The results of this study could help guide public health measures and vaccination strategies in response to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
elements.reason: The Conclusion provides an interpretation of the results and their implications for public health and vaccination strategies.
The abstract does not state the funding source; funding is reported only in the main text Funding section.
The abstract does not report the registry name or registration number; PROSPERO registration (CRD42023411778) appears only in the main text.

elements.quote: There is a significant increase in the number of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection reports in various countries. However, the trend of reinfection rate over time is not clear.
elements.reason: The abstract background describes the current state of knowledge (increasing reinfection reports) and explicitly identifies the key uncertainty (unclear trend of reinfection rate over time); the Introduction (text_4) further describes the global burden and ongoing mutation of SARS-CoV-2.

elements.quote: The results of this study could help guide public health measures and vaccination strategies in response to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained: the unclear time trend of reinfection motivates the meta-analysis, and results are framed as guiding public health measures and vaccination strategies.

Although the Discussion mentions advantages 'compared with the previous meta-analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate', no previous review is identified or cited in the Introduction, and the retrieved evidence does not show the need for the current review being justified relative to a cited prior review.
This is a review of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates (prognostic/prevalence evidence), not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action needs to be described.
The review does not evaluate complex interventions or delivery contexts, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time, so as to provide reference for the development of global unified reinfection standards and reinfection measures in the future.
elements.reason: The objectives are explicitly stated: to summarize current SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates across regions/populations and to examine time trends in reinfection rates. The objectives are clearly articulated, though not framed in a formal question framework; the aims are explicit and complete.
This is a review of reinfection rates (frequency estimation) with meta-regression, not a review of intervention effects, so planned PICO comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... reinfection working definition in this study was based on a positive laboratory result at least 90 days after laboratory confirmation of primary infection... The exclusion criteria were: (1) The sample size was less than 20; (2) Belonged to one of the following types of studies: editorial, case report, case series study, systematic review, meta-analysis, animal experiment, news report; (3) Secondary reporting or articles on repeated studies of the same population; (4) Grey literature
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly specifies eligibility criteria tied to the review question (estimating SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate), eligible study designs (cohort, case-control, descriptive/cross-sectional), a working definition of reinfection with a minimum 90-day interval between positive tests, and exclusion criteria including minimum sample size, prohibited study types, duplicate populations, and grey literature.

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language... (4) Original research. The exclusion criteria were: ... (4) Grey literature, including a range of documents not controlled by commercial publishing organizations.
elements.reason: Language criteria (no language limit, with translation procedures) and publication status (original research only; grey literature excluded) are reported, but no restriction or criterion regarding dissemination year/publication date is specified.

elements.quote: One of them reported only the reinfection rate, but not the associated number of first infections as well as the number of reinfections... Therefore, we excluded the above literature with the number of unreported infections
elements.reason: The review reports excluding a study because required numbers were not reported, but it does not explicitly distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country, and we also used spline regression to fit time-varying reinfection rates that did not account for heterogeneity. In addition, considering the change in the reinfection rate over time, we constructed a multiple meta-regression using the time interval between two positive tests as the independent variable, to estimate the time-varying reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The synthesis groups are specified (subgroups by age, variant, country, study population, and study type per Table 1 and text_10) and are linked to the review objectives of summarizing reinfection rates across regions/populations and examining trends over time via meta-regression on the time interval between infections.

elements.quote: In order to avoid data heterogeneity in metaanalysis while ensuring data quantity, we used previous literature and previous definitions of reinfection in some countries as the criteria for included literature and data extraction in this study.
elements.reason: Rationales are provided for some notable restrictions, e.g., the 90-day reinfection definition is based on WHO and US CDC guidance (text_7) and was chosen to avoid heterogeneity while ensuring data quantity (text_19), and grey literature exclusion is acknowledged in the limitations; however, no rationale is given for other restrictions such as the minimum sample size of 20.

elements.reason: The search end date (March 16, 2023) is explicitly reported as the date up to which sources were searched, consistent with 'as of March 16, 2023' and the abstract's 'up to March 16, 2023'.

elements.reason: The manuscript reports the method used to translate non-English articles during the screening/data collection process.

elements.reason: The main outcome (SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate) is identifiable and a working definition of reinfection is provided (positive result at least 90 days after primary infection), but outcome domains are not explicitly listed and defined as such; only extracted data items are enumerated.

No evidence of changes to processes for selecting results within outcome domains is reported.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists all data items sought during extraction, including participant/study characteristics.

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The authors describe an assumption/imputation rule for handling missing (unclear) information on reinfection variants.

No tool or guidance (e.g., a data extraction template or standard) used to determine which data items to collect is cited; the extraction form is referenced only as Additional file 3 without citing a source tool.

elements.quote: We used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) to evaluate the literature quality of cohort and case-control studies, and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool (JBI) for cross-sectional studies (Additional file 4).
elements.reason: Both risk-of-bias tools (NOS and JBI) are named and matched to study designs.

elements.quote: When the star rating in NOS was less than 3, or the number of 'yes' in JBI was less than 5 [23], we categorized the paper as 'high risk of bias'.
elements.reason: Only scoring thresholds are reported; the domains/items of the NOS and JBI tools are not described (possibly in Additional file 4, but not in the retrieved evidence).

elements.quote: When the star rating in NOS was less than 3, or the number of 'yes' in JBI was less than 5 [23], we categorized the paper as 'high risk of bias'.
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgement ('high risk of bias') is made and the rules (score thresholds) for deriving it are reported.
No adaptation of an existing risk-of-bias tool is reported; standard NOS and JBI tools were used as-is.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; only established tools (NOS, JBI) were applied.

elements.quote: Risk bias assessment was performed by two independent reviewers (H-XY, C-MS), and inconsistencies were judged by other independent reviewers (CY, Z-WH).
elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two), independence, and disagreement-resolution by other independent reviewers are reported.
No process for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators is reported; no indication such contact was attempted.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are mentioned; assessment was performed manually by reviewers.

elements.quote: We used meta-analysis to evaluate the pooled rate of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in the included studies... Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The effect measure (pooled reinfection rate/proportion, presented with 95% CIs) is specified for the single outcome, including the logit transformation used in synthesis.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the size of the reinfection rate effect are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: when the rate is close to 0 or 1, two problems will occur in the meta-regression: the confidence interval may exceed the interval of 0-1, and the variance is squeezed towards 0. Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution... we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The manuscript describes re-expressing the synthesized proportion via four candidate transformations (log, logit, arcsine, double arcsine) and selecting logit, with results in Additional file 5.

elements.quote: Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation (see Additional file 5 for specific results)
elements.reason: The choice of the logit transformation as effect measure is justified by statistical problems with rates near 0 or 1 and by post-transformation hypothesis testing.

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers (ZT Y-CH).
elements.reason: The methods describe explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (reinfection definition, study designs, sample size, exclusion of reviews/case reports, etc.), independent screening by named reviewers with conflict resolution, and subgroup/meta-regression synthesis grouping by variant, country, study type, and time interval, which together describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes data preparation for synthesis, including conversion of reinfection rates via four transformations and selection of logit transformation. Additional data handling is described in text_7 (e.g., classifying reinfection variants by WHO standards when not reported, calculating rates from provided data).

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1
elements.reason: Tables are referenced (Table 1 subgroup analysis results, Additional files for meta-analysis results), but the Methods section does not describe the tabular structures or the data included in them; table content is only evident from the Results.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was also performed to obtain reinfection rates and forest plots according to age, variant, and country.
elements.reason: The Methods mention forest plots for subgroup analyses, and Results reference forest plots (Additional file 6) and meta-regression figures (Fig. 5), but graphical methods such as meta-regression and spline plots are not described in the Methods section.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively
elements.reason: The grouping of studies in Table 1 is implicitly defined by subgroup categories (age, variant, country, population, study type), but no explicit statement of the basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs is provided.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation.
elements.reason: A rationale is given for the logit transformation in the statistical analysis, but no rationale is reported for any non-standard graphical displays (e.g., meta-regression or spline plots of time-varying rates).

elements.quote: All analyses were performed using R statistical software (version 4.2.3).
elements.reason: Software and version number for the statistical synthesis are explicitly reported.
A meta-analysis was performed, so no alternative synthesis method needed to be described.

elements.quote: If heterogeneity was low, a fixed-effects model was used to combine rates and correction estimates from different studies. Otherwise, a random-effects model was used.
elements.reason: Model choice (fixed- vs random-effects) is reported with a rationale based on heterogeneity level.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The statistical method for pooling rates (logit transformation of proportions) is described, along with meta-regression and subgroup analysis methods.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between studies was expressed using Cochran's Q statistic test ( P < 0.05) as well as I 2 > 50%.
elements.reason: Methods to identify and quantify heterogeneity (Cochran's Q and I-squared with thresholds) are reported.
A random-effects model was used, but the between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird, REML) is not reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
The method used to calculate confidence intervals for the summary effect under the random-effects model is not reported.
